en.title: Resident Evil Movie Drops Surprise Dead by Daylight Easter Egg
en.summary: Zach Cregger's new take on the iconic survival horror franchise is delighting fans with its faithfulness to the games. But one scene has players of a different beloved horror title doing a double-take.
en.body:
The latest **Resident Evil** movie, directed by **Zach Cregger**, has officially landed, and it's proving to be a thrilling ride for fans of the classic Capcom games. Despite not featuring familiar faces from the game series, Cregger's vision immerses viewers in the desperate struggle of a medical courier named Bryan, navigating a terrifying biomedical outbreak. Early reactions highlight the film's success in capturing the palpable tension and resourcefulness that defines the **Resident Evil** experience, from scavenging for ammo to the dreaded padlocked doors and grotesque mutant encounters.

What's truly exciting is how Cregger has woven in nods to the gaming world that extend beyond just his chosen franchise. During a particularly harrowing sequence, Bryan finds himself pursued by a mutated antagonist through the snow. As he attempts to evade her, he circles an overturned police car in a desperate maneuver. This specific action is a direct and hilarious call-out to players of **Dead by Daylight**, the popular asymmetrical multiplayer survival horror game. In **Dead by Daylight**, this evasive tactic is known as "looping," where a Survivor repeatedly runs around an environmental object to outmaneuver a Killer, buying precious time for teammates to complete objectives and ultimately escape.

## A Nod to Survivors Everywhere

This unexpected **Dead by Daylight** reference is more than just a fleeting visual gag; it's a testament to Cregger's understanding of the broader horror gaming landscape. For fans who spend hours in games like **Dead by Daylight**, "looping" is an intuitive, often life-saving strategy. Seeing this tactic mirrored in a **Resident Evil** film demonstrates a deep appreciation for player-driven mechanics and the meta-language that emerges from dedicated gaming communities. It’s a clever wink that acknowledges the shared DNA of survival horror across different platforms and experiences, making the film resonate with a wider audience of passionate gamers.

## The Resident Evil Legacy Continues

With **Resident Evil** already generating significant buzz, the inclusion of such an insightful Easter egg suggests that **Zach Cregger** and his team are committed to honoring the spirit of the games in every possible way. While details about future installments remain under wraps, this film's reception indicates a strong appetite for well-crafted entries in the **Resident Evil** universe that respect its history and engage its dedicated fanbase. The blend of familiar survival horror tropes with surprising, genre-spanning references is a recipe for success that fans will undoubtedly be eager to see more of.

content_raw: This article contains minor spoilers for Resident Evil Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is finally out and thrilling audiences everywhere with its unique blend of laughs and scares. The director’s spin on the popular Capcom video game series has also delighted many fans who weren’t sure how much of the true Resident Evil experience they would get, since Cregger chose not to include characters from the games in his reboot. Instead, the film follows a medical courier named Bryan, who is more like a random NPC than a Leon S. Kennedy type. Ultimately, there was no need to worry; Cregger proved he knew ball . Beyond finding ammo, battling with padlocked doors, and being chased by mutant creatures, some have also been pleasantly surprised by how the movie captures the real tension of playing the Resident Evil games. But among the familiar situations and panic moments the movie puts poor Bryan through, there’s also a fun moment that should please fans of an entirely different video game. During a scene where Bryan investigates an overturned cop car, only to find the mutated woman inside briefly gone, he eventually has to figure out how to escape her on foot in the snow. This leads to a hilarious shot of him “looping” around the cop car as she relentlessly chases him, a scene that will be extremely familiar to Dead by Daylight players. In the popular multiplayer survival horror game, “looping” is a tactic where a Survivor repeatedly runs around a structure or obstacle to evade the Killer during a chase. It’s a go-to move for wasting the Killer’s time while avoiding being hit, often giving the Survivor’s teammates an added opportunity to “pop” a generator and increase their chances of escaping the map. Resident Evil has become one of Dead by Daylight ’s most substantial crossover partnerships in the last five years. Developer Behaviour Interactive first collaborated with the franchise back in 2021, when Leon S. Kennedy and Jill Valentine were added as Survivors, Nemesis as a Killer, and the Raccoon City Police Department became a new map. Nemesis’s zombies and the ability for Survivors to interact with typewriters were also introduced, among other Resident Evil-themed elements and perks. The collab continued in 2022, adding Ada Wong and Rebecca Chambers as Survivors and Albert Wesker as a Killer, along with another version of the RPD map. While it’s currently unclear if Cregger actually meant to include the “looping” moment in his reboot movie as a direct reference to Dead by Daylight (feel free to confirm or deny in the comments, Zach!), it will surely have amused those who don’t just associate Resident Evil with the mainline game series and the movie adaptations, but with the franchise’s ongoing Dead by Daylight collaboration as well.
